parsed.explanation: The explicit crime of 'imitating the opposite sex' was struck down in 2022, removing the clearest universal-exposure statute. But the record shows dress-code policing and official discrimination against trans people persisting after the ruling, a still-enforced sodomy law (Art. 193, up to 7 years) with documented prosecutions, strict public-morality enforcement, censorship of LGBTQ material, no legal recognition, no advocacy infrastructure and no working recourse. No border-screening regime or mandatory marker disclosure is documented, so entry exposure is an open question rather than a known one. Trans-specific violence is undocumented. The operative regime is discretionary police and morality enforcement against visibly gender-nonconforming people, with a severe custodial tail for those read as same-sex couples — High Risk, not the catastrophic tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No implemented entry-screening or marker-disclosure regime is documented; the 2013 subregional 'testing' proposal was disavowed and never shown to operate.
entry_documents.protection: Visitors use home-issued passports; no documented border practice targeting trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Absence of documented screening is an open question, not a proven protection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Dress-code policing outlasted the 2022 ruling; a 2017 case saw a person held two weeks for 'looking too feminine'; morality laws are strictly enforced with documented LGBTQ prosecutions.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Constitutional Court struck down Art. 199 bis in 2022, removing the express cross-dressing offence.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Judicial invalidation did not end the discretionary police stops that preceded it.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Gender segregation and enforced dress codes documented; gender-segregation decisions at the national university.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rules operate through national institutions with no documented visitor exception.

care_services.exposure: Foreign nationals found HIV-positive are deported; no trans-specific or minor-specific care provisions documented.
care_services.interaction: Health discovery can trigger removal, a distinct traveller-facing exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Public morality laws strictly enforced; LGBTQ content blocked by the communications regulator; films banned; no legal gender recognition; ombudsman urged outright repeal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National human-rights ombudsman documents and criticises the practice.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Ombudsman findings have not changed police conduct, per 2023 assessment.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific rule documented; a trans minor accompanying a guardian faces the same segregation and morality-enforcement climate.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Official discrimination against trans people persisted in 2023; no trans-specific violence data or comparative baseline in the record.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No LGBTQ association exists to assist victims; a 2007 registration application went unanswered.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Without advocacy infrastructure, reporting to police is the only recourse and police are the documented discriminators.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether Art. 199 bis was legislatively repealed is unresolved; scale of post-2022 dress-code policing unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: One successful Constitutional Court challenge and an active ombudsman.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Judicial relief exists but has not produced recognition or protection in practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia's unwritten stop-and-search of trans visitors, passport confiscation and unofficial files resembles this dossier's persisting dress-code policing and official discrimination. Here the express cross-dressing offence has been judicially struck down, but an enforced sodomy law with documented prosecutions adds a custodial tail Karthovia lacks; overall comparable, marginally lower.

Varnalia's weekly raids, fines and payment demands are more systematic and repetitive than this record documents post-2022; this dossier shows persisting discrimination but no sourced enforcement figures. Varnalia sits lower; this jurisdiction is above it.

Kestrel Isles describes administrative border screening with refused admission and appeal desks — a documented, bounded process. This dossier documents no border regime at all, but has a harsher domestic morality-enforcement and custodial backdrop, placing it materially below Kestrel Isles.

parsed.synthesis: The 2022 Constitutional Court ruling removed the express criminalisation of gender-nonconforming presentation, which is the single largest positive in the record. It did not remove the policing: official discrimination, dress-code stops and strict morality enforcement persist, and Article 193's enforced same-sex provision creates a severe custodial exposure for a trans visitor read as part of a same-sex couple. With no legal recognition, no advocacy infrastructure, censored LGBTQ material and no documented border screening, the operative regime is discretionary police and morality enforcement with a severe tail — High Risk, above the systematic-administrative 0.35 anchors only because the cross-dressing offence itself is gone.
